description: **You don't have to be the best. You have to be the only.** "So what makes you different from the other forty people we're seeing this week?" If that question makes your stomach drop, you're not alone. You were told to pick a lane and climb, so you bought another course, earned another certificate, and still ended up on the same crowded rung as everyone else. Meanwhile, the things that actually set you apart, the odd summer job, the hobby, the language your grandmother taught you, never made it onto the résumé. **Climbing one ladder keeps you in the crowd. Stacking skills gets you out of it.** *Become One of One* is a practical, research-backed guide to skill stacking: combining a few good-enough skills, on purpose, into something rare, useful, and hard to replace. Peter Hollins walks you through a four-move method, See It, Stack It, Build It, Prove It, that turns the skills you already have into a category with exactly one member in it. title: The Rejection Sensitive Dysphoria Workbook for ADHD: A Practical Step-by-Step Guide to Man
description: Does an unanswered text have the power to ruin your entire evening? Does Any of This Sound Familiar? • You reread a short reply until the words stop making sense • One piece of feedback at work can wreck your whole day • You apologize before knowing if you did anything wrong • A friend's delayed reply becomes proof they're pulling away • You say yes to everything, then quietly resent all of it • You know you're overreacting, and knowing changes nothing I get it. It's midnight and you're still replaying an eleven-word message, trying to hear the tone it was written in. You've tried caring less, thinking positive, telling yourself it's no big deal. If rejection, criticism, or a sudden silence can hijack your whole day, and overthinking keeps you stuck long after everyone else moved on, this workbook was written for the brain you actually have. I've been there. I know how heavy it gets. • Clinical books explain the science, then leave you alone at midnight with your phone • "Just care less" advice targets the feeling, and the feeling was never the problem • Generic anxiety workbooks weren't built for a brain where emotions arrive before the brakes • This workbook gives you what those left out: a step-by-step system to catch the spiral earlier and choose what happens next. But First, a Warning This book only works in pen. If you want something that describes you perfectly and asks nothing back, this isn't it. Every section ends with a full page of guided work on your real triggers, because vague self-knowledge collapses under pressure and specific self-knowledge survives it. How to Think Bigger: Aim Higher, Get More Motivated, and Accomplish Big Things
description: How to Get More Motivated, Set Bigger Goals, and Achieve More by Thinking Bigger Have you ever wondered what separates people who think bigger from people who set their bar low? What makes one person accept low standards and another person to constantly raise them? Why does one person strive to build an international organization affecting the lives of millions of people, while another person is content working her entire life as a clerk? (Not that there’s anything wrong with being a clerk!) Why is one person challenging herself to run marathons, train her body and get fitter, while another is happy living a sedentary, unhealthy lifestyle? What drives a person who’s optimizing every single aspect of her life and what causes another person to maintain the status quo? You can say, “Well, the answer is simple enough – one person is ambitious, while the other one is not.” But what exactly causes it? And most importantly – how do you become more ambitious and think bigger? Is it something you’re born with and can’t change, or is it something over which you have control? I found this topic so fascinating I decided to find out the answer for myself and write a book about it. This book is the result of my research about people who think big and the science of being more ambitious. Here are just some of the things you will learn from the book: - What key things you need to inspire yourself to think bigger , and more importantly, achieve your big goals. - Why you need a “why,” and what kind of motivators will set you up for success (hint: attaining money or status are some of the least motivating goals possible). - The single most important thing to thinking bigger.
